newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end firmer, fail to break resistance.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end firmer, fail to break resistance.

text.p: Swiss shares closed firmer but below the day's highs, just failing to break resistance around 3,875 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI).

Trading volume rose in the second half of the session with short-covering ahead of Friday's expiry on the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex) as well as a friendly beginning on Wall Street buoyed Swiss shares, a dealer said.
"We may seen a friendly tendency and even reach new highs next week," a dealer said. Another trader warned the SMI may slip to 3,780 before rising again.
The SMI ended 23.6 points higher, or 0.61 percent, to 3,874.0 and the all share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 11.73 points, or 0.48 percent, to 2,471.62 points.

Ciba and Sandoz, which on Tuesday received U.S. approval to merge to Novartis, closed mixed after showing a friendly tendency throughout the day. Ciba registered shares slid two francs to 1,623. Sandoz edged up three francs to 1,525. The companies said that Novartis shares will be traded on the Swiss bourse on December 23 for the first time.
Roche certificates added 70 francs to 10.070 on short covering. Short covering also led Nestle up, which posted gains of more than two percent to 1,410 francs.
Holderbank, Surveillance and SMH posted gains, profiting from the U.S. dollar's strenght.

Insurer Baloise continued its weak bias, slumping 2.17 percent to 2,700 francs amid some disappointment the company did not announce a takeover on Tuesday. Winterthur was flat at 766 francs. Major banks CS Holding, UBS and SBC advanced.
Swissair surged 18 francs to 1,087 ahead of Thursday's press conference.
Second-tier Biber slumped 4.60 francs to 0.30 after saying its debt is covered by 40 percent on Tuesday.
